"def KL_divergence(p, q):
    '''
    Input
    p: probability distributions, 1-dimensional numpy array (or list) of floats
    q: probability distributions, 1-dimensional numpy array (or list) of floats
    Output
    divergence: KL-divergence of two probability distributions, a single scalar value (float)
    '''
    p = np.asarray(p, dtype=float)
    q = np.asarray(q, dtype=float)
    mask = p > 0
    div = np.zeros_like(p)
    # Handle cases where p>0 and q>0
    valid = mask & (q > 0)
    div[valid] = p[valid] * np.log2(p[valid] / q[valid])
    # Cases where p>0 and q==0 contribute infinite divergence
    div[mask & (q == 0)] = np.inf
    return np.sum(div)


def mutual_info(channel, prior):
    '''
    Input
    channel: a classical channel, 2d array of floats; channel[i][j] means probability of i given j
    prior:   input random variable, 1d array of floats.
    Output
    mutual: mutual information between the input random variable and the random variable associated with the output of the channel, a single scalar value (float)
    '''
    channel = np.array(channel, dtype=float)
    prior = np.array(prior, dtype=float)
    n_y, n_x = channel.shape

    # Output distribution p_Y(y) = sum_x p(y|x) p_X(x)
    p_Y = channel @ prior

    # Joint distribution p_XY(x,y) = p_X(x) * p(y|x)
    p_XY = prior[:, None] * channel.T  # shape (n_x, n_y)

    # Entropy function (using log base 2, treating 0*log2(0) as 0)
    def entropy(p):
        p = np.asarray(p, dtype=float)
        mask = p > 0
        return -np.sum(p[mask] * np.log2(p[mask]))

    H_X = entropy(prior)
    H_Y = entropy(p_Y)
    H_XY = entropy(p_XY.flatten())

    mutual = H_X + H_Y - H_XY
    return float(mutual)


def blahut_arimoto(channel, e):
    '''
    Input
    channel: a classical channel, 2d array of floats; Channel[i][j] means probability of i given j
    e:       error threshold, a single scalar value (float)
    Output
    rate_new: channel capacity, a single scalar value (float)
    '''
    channel = np.array(channel, dtype=float)
    n_y, n_x = channel.shape

    # Initialize random prior distribution over inputs
    p = np.random.rand(n_x)
    p = p / np.sum(p)

    while True:
        # Output distribution induced by current prior
        p_Y = channel @ p

        # Compute KL divergences D(p(Y|x)||p_Y) for each input x
        D = np.empty(n_x)
        for i in range(n_x):
            D[i] = KL_divergence(channel[:, i], p_Y)

        # Current mutual information (rate)
        rate_old = np.sum(p * D)

        # Update prior according to Blahut-Arimoto rule
        expD = np.exp(D)
        p_new = p * expD
        Z = np.sum(p_new)
        p_new = p_new / Z

        # Output distribution for the new prior
        p_Y_new = channel @ p_new

        # Compute KL divergences for the new output distribution
        D_new = np.empty(n_x)
        for i in range(n_x):
            D_new[i] = KL_divergence(channel[:, i], p_Y_new)

        # Updated rate (mutual information for new prior)
        rate_new = np.sum(p_new * D_new)

        # Check convergence
        if abs(rate_new - rate_old) < e:
            return float(rate_new)

        # Prepare for next iteration
